sources.entry: Earshot - Live on-device transcription of any app you pick, with speaker names in Microsoft Teams.

summary.one_liner: Earshot is a macOS menu bar app that live-transcribes the audio of any app you pick (Teams, Zoom, Chrome, Discord, etc.) on-device, with speaker names in Microsoft Teams.
summary.what_it_does: Earshot lists the apps currently playing sound in the menu bar; choosing one captures only that app's audio via Core Audio process taps and transcribes it live with whisper.cpp (Metal), cutting audio at pauses and skipping silence. An optional "Include my microphone" setting transcribes your own voice under your name. In Microsoft Teams, speaker names are taken from Teams' Live Captions panel read through the accessibility API. Sessions are filed under the matching calendar event (via EventKit) and saved as Transcript.txt and Audio.m4a, with Markdown and .srt export from the Library. An optional live subtitles window offers two engines: Apple's on-device SpeechAnalyzer ("Fast") or Kyutai STT 1B on MLX ("High", a 2.4 GB download). The interface is available in English and French.
use_cases: Transcribe a Teams or Zoom meeting locally without a bot joining the call
Get named speaker transcripts from Microsoft Teams captions
Record and transcribe university classes filed by calendar event
Show live subtitles for audio playing on the Mac
Export meeting transcripts to Markdown or SRT subtitles
Make class transcripts searchable alongside other documents
how_to_run: Download Earshot.dmg from the releases, open it and drag Earshot to Applications
Open Earshot from Applications and approve it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway (not notarized)
Build from source: scripts/build.sh --install (Command Line Tools only)
Test on a file: build/Earshot.app/Contents/MacOS/Earshot --transcribe some-recording.wav
notable: Captures a single app's audio output rather than the whole system or the microphone
Runs fully on-device; audio never leaves the Mac
Speaker names from Teams' live captions via the accessibility API
Sessions saved as plain text files that folder indexers like doc-indexer-macos can search
Two live subtitle engines: Apple's on-device recognition or Kyutai STT
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon
Not notarized by Apple; first launch needs manual approval in System Settings
Speaker names only work with Microsoft Teams; needs Accessibility-style permission and Teams captions on
High subtitles need a 2.4 GB download and Python 3.10–3.12 installed separately
